title: Adjustments and reasonable accommodations
summary: Adjustments at work, and support outside it, such as Access to Work, Personal Independence Payment and disability cards, with Eleni from our People Team answering questions.
plainSummary: In the UK, employers must make reasonable changes at work for disabled people, and that can include neurodivergent people. This chat covers support at work, and schemes outside it, such as Access to Work, Personal Independence Payment, Disability Living Allowance for children, and disability and carer cards. These can really help, but they can be slow and hard to get. Eleni from our People Team then answered questions about support at giffgaff.

title: AI

title: Special interests
summary: What special interests are, why they matter so much to neurodivergent people, how they’re often dismissed, and how to respond well to them.
plainSummary: A special interest is a subject someone cares about very deeply. They’re common in autistic people and people with ADHD. They can help people feel calm and in control, and can lead to real expertise. But people are often told to stop talking about them, so many learn to hide them. To help, take the interest seriously, ask about it, and listen.

title: Early versus late diagnosis
summary: The differences between being diagnosed as neurodivergent early or later in life, in the support people get and how they see themselves.
plainSummary: Some people find out they’re neurodivergent as children, and some only as adults. An early diagnosis can mean support at school, but girls, children of colour and children from poorer families are often missed. A late diagnosis can bring relief, and also sadness about the years without help. Support for adults is harder to get. If someone tells you about their diagnosis, be curious and open.

title: Interoception and proprioception
summary: Interoception and proprioception, the hidden senses for what’s happening inside your body and where it is, how they work differently for neurodivergent people, and how to support them.
plainSummary: We have more than 5 senses. Proprioception tells you where your body is without looking. Interoception tells you what’s happening inside your body, such as hunger, thirst or a racing heart. These senses often work differently in neurodivergent people. That can mean bumping into things, not noticing hunger until it’s urgent, or not spotting stress until it’s too much. Movement breaks, weighted blankets, reminders to eat and drink, and regular check-ins can help.

title: Families
summary: What life is like in a family with neurodivergent members: communication, routines, the strengths these families share, and what helps or harms family relationships.
plainSummary: A neurodiverse family is one where at least one person is neurodivergent. These families often need to work on how they talk to each other, and on routines that help without being too strict. They also have real strengths, like empathy, creative problem-solving and pride in being different. What helps is talking openly about needs, and accepting each other. What doesn’t help is strict rules, misunderstandings, and treating differences as problems.
